status: stage 1 implemented: the helper accepts a validated owner-only Unix socket and serves the unchanged IPC 6 protocol over it; the host still spawns the helper with --ipc, so production behaviour is unchanged until stage 2

validation: argument count exactly two; path absolute, UTF-8 bounded (<100 bytes), no NUL
parent directory must be a real directory (lstat), owned by the current uid, with no group/other permission bits
socket path must be a socket (lstat S_IFSOCK) owned by the current uid
connect must succeed and getpeereid() must return the current uid
on any failure exit 2 without falling back to stdio
on success dup2 the socket onto fd 0/1 and run the existing IPC 6 loop; the 20 s fuse still applies
implementation.host: unchanged in this stage; the darwin backend still uses OwnedProcess.spawn([helper, --ipc])

valid_transport.command: host UDS in a 0700 directory + open -n <installed app> --args --connect <path> + IPC 6 probe frame
valid_transport.result: ok=true, 2112-byte reply, connect 0.056 s on the installed build (0.309 s on the build-directory build)
valid_transport.permissions: all four denied under the LaunchServices/own identity (helper entries reset), as expected before the owner re-grants

negative_cases.case: missing socket in an owner-only directory
regular file instead of a socket

existing_path_unaffected.result: all four capabilities granted through the existing POSIX/host context; clean close
